subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` suppress explicit Gateway/control-plane `update.run` managed-service handoffs for supervised/headless Gateway installs, or remain limited to configured background `update.auto` applies?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs define the env var as a background-auto-update kill-switch, but the reported headless launchd use case wants an operator-wide update-restart block; automation cannot safely broaden that public contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Broaden the existing kill-switch
options.body: Make `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` reject or skip Gateway-originated managed `update.run` handoffs before any restart handoff is created, and update docs/tests for that expanded contract.

options.title: Keep the current split
options.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` scoped to configured background auto-updates and document that explicit `update.run` remains an operator/requested update path.

options.title: Add a separate explicit update-run guard
options.body: Introduce a distinct operator guard for control-plane `update.run` restarts so background auto-update policy and explicit update commands do not share one ambiguous variable.

recommendation.title: Keep the current split
recommendation.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` scoped to configured background auto-updates and document that explicit `update.run` remains an operator/requested update path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current kill-switch behavior and are the clearest owner signal for deciding whether its public scope should expand.
